review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions of `encoded`, `cost`, `Message` and `retained` in PivotTree.lean. I grepped the Trees directory and the wider repo for `@[simp]` and for other uses of the `encoded`/`cost` unfolding pattern. PivotTree.lean has no simp lemmas for `encoded` or `cost` on `node` trees. The same unfolding recipe appears in TreeOmissionLaw.lean (lines 43 and 48) and in this file. I found no loop, competing-rule or direction problem, and the file declares no simp attributes. The one finding is about a missing simp interface and is a modest, maintainability-level issue. I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas are untested.

findings.problem: PivotTree.lean has no simp lemmas for `encoded` or `cost` on node trees. Every proof about a node therefore case-splits on `enc a c (ω.1 c)`, rewrites with `he`, and unfolds the definitions by hand. The recipe `simp only [encoded,he,Option.map_none/some,cost,…]` appears four times in this file (lines 26, 38, 54, 59) and twice more in TreeOmissionLaw.lean (lines 43, 48). Each call also has to list the arithmetic cast lemmas (`Nat.cast_add`, `Nat.cast_one`, `mul_zero`, `zero_add`) as extras. The canonical forms are therefore not stated anywhere, and each proof depends on the exact shape produced by unfolding the structural-recursion equations.
findings.proposed_change: In PivotTree.lean, next to `encoded` and `cost`, add equation lemmas for the encoded node, split by the `enc` result. One pair covers the `none` case: `encoded … (.node a l r) ω c = none` and `cost … (encoded … (.node a l r) ω c) = 0` given `enc a c (ω.1 c) = none`. The other pair covers the `some m` case: `encoded … = some ⟨m, encoded … l …, encoded … r …⟩` and `cost … = lc a c (ω.1 c) m + cost … (encoded … l …) + cost … (encoded … r …)` given `enc a c (ω.1 c) = some m`. Tag them `@[simp]`. The hypothesis `enc … = some m` is a variable-headed equation on the left, so it should be used as a side condition that simp can discharge from `he`. Also add `@[simp] cost_nil`. The proofs then reduce to `simp [encoded_node_some, he]`, and the same lemmas serve TreeOmissionLaw.lean.
findings.benefit: The unfolding recipe sits in one place instead of six copies. Cost and encoded terms on nodes normalise to a stated form (local cost plus the two subtree costs), and downstream proofs no longer depend on how the equation compiler unfolds `Option.map`. If `encoded` or `cost` changes, only the lemmas need updating.
